claim: For \(F(t)=a+b e^{2\pi i t}+c e^{4\pi i t}\) on \(\mathbb T\) with normalized Haar measure, the sharp inequality \(\|F\|_8\le K_8(|a|^2+|b|^2+|c|^2)^{1/2}\) has \(K_8^8=\Psi(\tau_*)\), where \(\Psi(\tau)=(70\tau^4+560\tau^3+420\tau^2+56\tau+1)/(1+2\tau)^4\) and \(\tau_*\) is the unique positive root of \(35\tau^3-21\tau-2=0\). Equivalently, \(K_8^8\) is the unique positive root of \(1331X^3+403851X^2-4842915X-13488475=0\), numerically \(K_8^8=13.787723967226097408\ldots\) and \(K_8=1.388150559666132350\ldots\). Every nonzero extremizer, and only those extremizers, satisfies \(|a|=|c|\), \(|a|^2=\tau_*|b|^2\), and \(\arg a+\arg c-2\arg b\equiv0\pmod{2\pi}\); equivalently, up to a nonzero scalar and character modulation, it is \(\sqrt{\tau_*}+z+\sqrt{\tau_*}z^2\).

correctness.rationale: Parseval converts the eighth moment to the squared coefficient norm of F^4. Coefficientwise triangle inequalities give the exact phase-alignment condition. The aligned moment expands exactly in A=a^2+c^2, B=b^2 and R=ac with strictly positive R-derivative, forcing equal endpoint magnitudes. Boundary faces have eighth-power ratio at most 35/8. Homogeneity then leaves the one-variable rational function Psi, whose derivative factors exactly as -24(35 tau^3-21 tau-2)/(1+2 tau)^5. The cubic has one positive root and the derivative changes from positive to negative there, giving the unique global maximum. The equality conditions are therefore necessary and sufficient.

value.rationale: The consecutive three-frequency spectrum is the smallest spectrum with a nontrivial additive relation and is a canonical test object for Lambda(p) constants. The result determines a natural exact operator norm, proves that the p=8 optimizer has a nontrivial magnitude ratio rather than equal coefficients, and classifies every extremizer. This supplies structural information about how additive resonance and amplitude balancing interact, rather than a phase-only or numerical table entry.
